newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: 25 jailed for 1,000 years for Colombian massacre.
newsitem.headline: 25 jailed for 1,000 years for Colombian massacre.

text.p: A judge in Medellin, Colombia's third largest city, sentenced 25 people on Thursday to jail terms totalling more than 1,000 years for one of Colombia's worst-ever massacres, judicial sources said.

The 25-strong gang were convicted of massacring 35 people in January 1994 at a party in a squatter camp known as La Chinita in Apartado, one of the main towns in the trouble-torn banana-growing region of Uraba in northwest Colombia.
The judge handed down terms of between six and 51 years to the group, which included former regional leaders of the Communist Party and suspected leftist guerrillas.
The attack was blamed on the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), Latin America's oldest and largest guerrilla army.

Most of the dead were members of the Hope, Peace and Liberty movement -- a political organisation founded by former rebels of the Maoist-inspired People's Liberation Army (EPL), who in 1990 laid down their arms and returned to civilian life.

Hope, Peace and Liberty had dominated the main banana workers' union and forged close ties with the plantation bosses, thereby depriving the FARC of its political powerbase in the region and sparking a bitter struggle for control.
But the judge cleared Jose Antonio Lopez Bula, a member of the left-wing patriotic Union party and mayor of Apartado at the time of the massacre.
Another former Apartado mayor, Nelson Campo, was cleared of taking part in the massacre but sentenced to six years' jail for rebellion.
